## Foundations of Clinical Research: From Clinical Question to Publication

**Organisation:** Neudata — *#ClearDataClearImpact*

> **Outline only — module materials will be developed on demand, after the 8-session course has run.**
> The 8-session course takes participants from a clinical question to a draft manuscript, with the analyses run by instructors. These optional modules are for smaller groups who want to go further: doing the analyses themselves, or learning a specialised method that the course only introduced.


* * *

## 1. How the modules work

| | |
|---|---|
| **Who** | Graduates of the 8-session course, 6–12 per module. Each module can run on its own; they need not be taken in order. |
| **Format** | 1–2 sessions of 3 hours each (the same rhythm as the course), plus 3–6 hours of homework on the participant's own project or a course dataset. |
| **Software** | R and RStudio on participants' own laptops (free). The hands-on modules assume the free Neudata course ***Clinical Data Analysis in R*** has been completed. |
| **Data** | FLUID-ICU (the course dataset) for practice, then the participant's own data where ethics approval and data-protection rules allow. Purpose-built teaching datasets for the meta-analysis and diagnostic-accuracy modules. |
| **Output** | Every module ends with a concrete product: a reproducible script, an analysis section, a forest plot, a model report or a checklist-based appraisal. |
| **Link to the course** | The course *introduced* each topic (shown as "Course link" below); the module turns it into hands-on practice. |


* * *

## 2. Module A — Hands-on R analysis of your own data

**Course link:** Sessions 5–6 (data cleaning, Table 1, tests, regression, Kaplan–Meier/Cox, missing data — all demonstrated by the instructor) and the FLUID-ICU R scripts.

**Aims.** Participants will be able to (1) import, clean and document a real dataset reproducibly, with a cleaning log; (2) produce Table 1 and publication-quality figures; (3) run and check the analyses in a pre-written statistical analysis plan (tests, linear/logistic regression, Kaplan–Meier and Cox, a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis); and (4) export results into the manuscript template.

**Prerequisites.** Completion of the 8-session course; *Clinical Data Analysis in R* completed; a laptop with R and RStudio; ideally a dataset of one's own (or a proposal from the course that has collected data) with ethics approval and a written SAP.

**Outline (2 sessions).**

| Session | Content | Product |
|---|---|---|
| A1 — From raw data to Table 1 | Reproduce the FLUID-ICU cleaning script line by line; adapt it to one's own data (duplicates, sentinel values, implausible values, derived variables); cleaning log; Table 1 and figures; version control and backups | Clean dataset + cleaning log + Table 1 for one's own data |
| A2 — From SAP to Results | Run the SAP: unadjusted comparisons, adjusted model (logistic, linear or Cox), checking assumptions, multiple imputation as sensitivity analysis; tables and forest plot; writing the statistical-methods paragraph | Results section draft + reproducible script |


* * *

## 3. Module B — Systematic review and meta-analysis

**Course link:** Sessions 3–4 (systematic reviews, PRISMA flow, forest plots, heterogeneity, risk-of-bias tools) and Session 2 (searching).

**Aims.** Participants will be able to (1) write a systematic-review protocol and register it in PROSPERO; (2) build a reproducible multi-database search and screen records in pairs; (3) extract data and assess risk of bias (RoB 2 or ROBINS-I); and (4) pool effect estimates (fixed vs random effects), interpret heterogeneity (I²) and draw a forest and funnel plot, reported with PRISMA 2020.

**Prerequisites.** Completion of the 8-session course; for the analysis part, *Clinical Data Analysis in R* (the meta-analysis is run with a ready-made script); a review question (PICO) agreed with the module lead.

**Outline (2 sessions).**

| Session | Content | Product |
|---|---|---|
| B1 — Protocol, search and screening | Review question and eligibility; PROSPERO; search strategy across databases; screening in pairs; PRISMA flow diagram; data-extraction form | Registered (or ready-to-register) protocol + search strategy |
| B2 — Bias, pooling and reporting | Risk-of-bias assessment; pooling ORs/RRs in R; fixed vs random effects; I² and subgroup ideas; funnel plot and small-study effects; certainty of evidence (GRADE, introduced); PRISMA 2020 | Forest plot + draft Results for a small teaching meta-analysis |


* * *

## 4. Module C — Prediction models and machine learning

**Course link:** Session 6 (overfitting, prediction vs explanation, calibration and discrimination, TRIPOD+AI introduced).

**Aims.** Participants will be able to (1) tell a prediction question from a causal question; (2) estimate the sample size needed to develop a model and avoid overfitting; (3) develop a simple logistic prediction model and assess discrimination (AUC) and calibration, with internal validation (bootstrapping); (4) understand what machine-learning methods add and where they mislead; and (5) appraise a published model with TRIPOD+AI and PROBAST.

**Prerequisites.** Completion of the 8-session course; *Clinical Data Analysis in R*; comfortable with logistic regression output.

**Outline (2 sessions).**

| Session | Content | Product |
|---|---|---|
| C1 — Building a model properly | Prediction vs causation; candidate predictors; sample size for prediction models; developing a logistic model on FLUID-ICU (28-day mortality); discrimination and calibration plots; bootstrapped internal validation | Model report with AUC, calibration plot and optimism-corrected performance |
| C2 — Machine learning and appraisal | Penalised regression and a tree-based method compared with logistic regression; data leakage and other pitfalls; external validation; fairness; reading a published AI/ML model with TRIPOD+AI and PROBAST | Structured appraisal of one published prediction or ML model |


* * *

## 5. Module D — Diagnostic-accuracy studies

**Course link:** Session 4 (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and prevalence, ROC curves, likelihood ratios, QUADAS-2 introduced).

**Aims.** Participants will be able to (1) design a diagnostic-accuracy study (index test, reference standard, spectrum of patients, blinding); (2) calculate sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and likelihood ratios with 95% CIs, and draw a ROC curve with its AUC; (3) choose a cut-off sensibly; and (4) report with STARD 2015 and appraise with QUADAS-2.

**Prerequisites.** Completion of the 8-session course. R is used only in the second half (a ready-made script); participants without R can follow with a spreadsheet calculator.

**Outline (1 session, optional second session for a project).**

| Session | Content | Product |
|---|---|---|
| D1 — Design, analysis and reporting | Diagnostic questions and designs; common biases (spectrum, verification, incorporation); 2×2 accuracy table with CIs; predictive values across prevalences; ROC/AUC and cut-offs in R (e.g. lactate for 28-day mortality in FLUID-ICU); STARD 2015 and QUADAS-2 | Completed accuracy analysis + STARD-based outline of a study |
| D2 (optional) — Your own diagnostic question | Protocol for a unit-level diagnostic-accuracy study, sample size for sensitivity/specificity, data-collection form | Protocol outline |


* * *

## 6. Module E — Advanced survival and longitudinal analysis

**Course link:** Session 6 (censoring, Kaplan–Meier, log-rank, Cox HR; demonstrated on FLUID-ICU Question 1).

**Aims.** Participants will be able to (1) fit and check Cox models (proportional-hazards assumption, time-varying effects); (2) handle competing risks (e.g. ICU discharge alive vs death) and immortal-time bias; (3) analyse repeated measurements over time (e.g. daily fluid balance or SOFA) with mixed-effects models; and (4) report these analyses clearly.

**Prerequisites.** Completion of the 8-session course; *Clinical Data Analysis in R*; Module A recommended.

**Outline (2 sessions).**

| Session | Content | Product |
|---|---|---|
| E1 — Beyond the basic Cox model | Checking proportional hazards; time-varying covariates; immortal-time bias; competing risks (cumulative incidence, Fine–Gray, introduced); reporting time-to-event results | Survival analysis of FLUID-ICU with PH checks and a competing-risk comparison |
| E2 — Longitudinal data | Long vs wide data; plotting trajectories; linear mixed-effects models for daily measurements; missing data in repeated measures; when to ask a statistician | Mixed-model analysis of daily fluid balance with a short Results paragraph |


* * *

## 7. Choosing a module

| If you want to… | Take |
|---|---|
| Analyse the data from your own project yourself | **A** (then E if your outcome is time-to-event or repeated) |
| Summarise all the evidence on a question | **B** |
| Build or judge a risk score, prediction tool or AI model | **C** |
| Test how good a test, score or sign is at detecting a condition | **D** |
| Go deeper on time-to-event or repeated-measures outcomes | **E** |

Key resources for each module are listed in `Course/References/further_reading.md` (Cochrane Handbook and PRISMA 2020 for B; TRIPOD+AI and the Riley sample-size paper for C; STARD 2015 and QUADAS-2 for D; *Statistics at Square One* and the Bland–Altman Statistics Notes for A and E).
